text:
michael.h: Heads-up — restore test for customer-tenant-42 failed during decrypt step. Error: "AccessDenied: kms:Decrypt" when pulling snapshot from s3://redwood-backups/prod/tenant-42/2026-03-20.snap

sara_sec: ack, can you paste the full error? any stack or logs?

michael.h: log snippet: `ERROR backup-restore - decrypt failed: AccessDeniedException: User: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/backup-restore does not have kms:Decrypt on key arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/abcd-ef01`

dan_engineer: that's the exact grant gap we feared after the RBAC change yesterday. We removed broad CMK grants and tightened to service-account roles. Apparently the backup job uses the backup-restore role, not service-account.

san_ops: @anita_ops you rolled the RBAC change?

anita_ops: I did a targeted policy lock-down for S3 and KMS earlier. I thought backup-restore role was in the allow list — looks like I missed the cross-account grant for the scheduled restore job. Sorry.

sara_sec: No blame — fix path: 1) grant kms:Decrypt for backup-restore principal on CMK, 2) run restore smoke test, 3) add CI check to catch missing grants. Also need audit trail entries (CloudTrail) for failed Decrypt.

dan_engineer: Quick mitigation idea: temporarily add a key policy statement allowing aws:sourceArn of the backup job lambda OR attach a grant via `aws kms create-grant`. Example grant command: ```aws kms create-grant --key-id arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/abcd-ef01 --grantee-principal arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/backup-restore --operations Decrypt,DescribeKey```

sara_sec: Good. Prefer key policy adjustments for long-term, grants for short window. Also record grant IDs in ticket.

ops-bot: incident-12345 created: "restore failure -> KMS decrypt denied" assigned to anita_ops, severity P2.

anita_ops: I'll apply a temporary grant now, run restore, then update the CMK key policy to include the backup-restore role and the scheduled-job principal. ETA 20m.

dan_engineer: After that, please run an end-to-end restore to a staging DB and verify decryption + data integrity. Use `aws s3 cp` to fetch the snapshot and `pg_restore` to load.

sara_sec: Also we should add an alert for repeated KMS Decrypt failures: CloudWatch metric filter on CloudTrail events where errorCode == "AccessDenied" && eventName == "Decrypt". Create PagerDuty for >3 failures in 5m.

anita_ops: noted. I'll create a runbook entry: steps to grant, verify, revoke temporary grants, and required audit logs to attach to tickets.

dan_engineer: Small long-term action: change backup job to assume a dedicated service account with explicit CMK access and add a terraform-managed grant so RBAC changes get tested in PR.

sara_sec: Also let's capture this as a vulnerability triage item — if an RBAC drift can block restores, make it a reliability risk. Add to security backlog: label `backup-restore-hardening`.

anita_ops: doing that now. creating ticket sec-2042 with checklist and linking incident.

michael.h: ran the restore after grant — decrypt succeeded, restore to staging completed. Data checksum matches. Thanks.

sara_sec: great. action items: [anita_ops] update CMK policy + remove temp grant, [dan_engineer] terraformize service-account + CI test, [sara_sec] create alert & backlog item. We'll do a 1-hour postmortem doc tomorrow AM. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: incident-12345 status -> mitigated by temporary grant; awaiting key policy update for closure.

kms-bot: CloudTrail event IDs logged: EVT-7890, EVT-7891 (Decrypt:AccessDenied) — attached to incident.

sara_sec: thanks everyone — good catch in the restore test. We'll keep RBAC strict but make restores resilient.

Notes/links: https://confluence.redwood/security/backup-restore-runbook, https://console.aws.amazon.com/kms/home, https://console.aws.amazon.com/cloudtrail/home
